description: Administer the index itself — one tool, one `action`. Nothing here answers a question about the CODE; that is dossier and search.

THREE THINGS SET `stale` AND EACH NEEDS A DIFFERENT RESPONSE, so read the `staleness` list rather than the boolean. `data` — the database is older than the source; `action='refresh'` fixes it. `schema` — the stamped build version against the one this server expects; when the INDEX IS NEWER no rebuild clears it, because rebuilding re-stamps the same newer version. `code` — this process is older than the working tree; only restarting the client replaces it, and a build through it is REFUSED rather than allowed to re-stamp the index with old pipeline logic, which can silently drop whole layers and then report health.
READS ARE UNAFFECTED BY THE `code` AXIS: query tools open the database per call, so the data in a reply is current even when this process is not. WRITES are what the refusal protects.

`action='status'` is the full diagnosis and costs a call — do not open a session with it. Every query reply already names its `target` and carries a `staleness` block if and only if there is one, so a current index costs nothing to establish and a stale one announces itself on the first reply you were going to make anyway.

A declaration is REFUSED BY NAME when it names an unknown section, with the allowed set — never applied partially and never silently ignored. `index(action='stats')` grades a named index; `action='cull'` deletes aged-out or version-stale databases.
